task.title: Clip elements
task.shortdesc: A clip cuts away the parts of an element that are outside an area. You draw the area with a clipPath element or you write it as a basic shape.

info.p: Define the area with a clipPath element and name it in the clip-path property of the element you want to clip, as url(#id). The parts of the element that are under the shapes of the clipPath stay visible, and the rest is cut away. You can set clip-path on shapes, text, images, groups and use elements.

A clipPath can hold shapes, text, and use elements that point to a shape or to text. The shapes together make one area, and the area is the union of all of them. Each shape is filled with its clip-rule, nonzero or evenodd, as fill-rule works for a fill. A child with display: none or visibility: hidden adds nothing. A clipPath that holds nothing cuts away the whole element.
The area follows the transforms. You can set a transform on the clipPath or on any of its shapes. The element that you clip carries its clip with it, so the clip moves when the element moves.
A clipPath and each of its shapes can have a clip-path too. The area is then the part of the shapes that is also inside that second clip.

By default the numbers in a clipPath are in user units. With clipPathUnits="objectBoundingBox" they are fractions of the box of the element that is clipped, so one clip fits elements of every size. A clip-path that names an element that is not a clipPath, or does not name anything, clips nothing.

stepxmp.pre: <defs> <clipPath id="lens" clipPathUnits="objectBoundingBox"> <circle cx="0.5" cy="0.5" r="0.4"/> </clipPath> </defs> <rect class="lensed" width="90" height="70" fill="#1d4f7a"/>

info.p: Instead of a clipPath you can write the shape in the property. The shape is measured in a reference box, which is the stroke box of the element unless you name another one. These are the shapes:

row.entry: A circle. The radius is a length, a percentage of the diagonal of the box divided by the square root of 2, or closest-side, farthest-side, closest-corner or farthest-corner. Without a radius it is closest-side. The center follows at, and it is the middle of the box without it. You can write the position with keywords and with offsets from an edge, as at right 10px bottom 5px.
An ellipse. The radii are lengths, percentages of the width and the height of the box, or the same keywords as for a circle. Without radii both are closest-side.

entry.codeph: inset(top right bottom left round radii)

row.entry: A rectangle that is smaller than the box by the given distances. One to four distances work like the margin of a box. After round you write one to four corner radii, and after a slash the vertical radii for elliptical corners. When the distances of two opposite sides are together longer than the box, CSSMedia reduces them in proportion until they fit.

entry.codeph: xywh(x y width height round radii)

row.entry: A rectangle given by its position and its size, measured from the top left corner of the box.

entry.codeph: rect(top right bottom left round radii)

row.entry: A rectangle given by the distances of its four sides from the top left corner of the box. A side can be auto, which is the side of the box.

entry.codeph: polygon(fill-rule round radius, x y, x y, ...)

row.entry: A polygon with its vertices, each a pair of lengths or percentages. The optional nonzero or evenodd sets the fill rule, and round with a length rounds the corners. A polygon with fewer than three vertices is not a shape and clips everything.
A path in the syntax of the d attribute of SVG, in a string. Its coordinates start at the top left corner of the box.

A path in CSS syntax. It starts at the point after from, and each command is move, line, hline, vline, curve, smooth, arc or close. to gives the end point from the top left corner of the box, and by gives it from the point where the command starts. A curve takes its control points after with.

fig.title: A rectangle clipped by five basic shapes

image.alt: Five rectangles with a dashed outline. Inside each one a dark blue shape remains: a circle, an ellipse, a rounded square, a triangle and a heart.

info.p: A word before or after the shape chooses the box that the shape is measured in:

ul.li: fill-box is the box of the shape without its outline. content-box and padding-box are the same box.
stroke-box is the box that also holds the outline. It is the box that CSSMedia uses when you name none. border-box and margin-box are the same box.
view-box is the whole drawing, from its top left corner.

info.p: A box without a shape clips to the edges of that box: clip-path: fill-box cuts away the outline of a shape. The value none, the initial one, does not clip.
